clue.text: Colourful creature, clever to follow goat

indicators.note: the clever word comes after the goat word in the answer

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed in the clue is itself a comma, read as the word
a goat is one that butts, hence a butter
fly is slang for sharp, knowing, clever

explanation.surface: A bright animal is described as clever enough to trail behind a goat.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma printed after 'creature' is not just punctuation: it is itself a piece of the wordplay, read as the word.
explanation.definitionFit: This butterfly, named for the white comma mark on its wing, is an orange-brown insect, a colourful creature.

clue.text: He wanted bottle of cordial, only laced with whiskey

indicators.note: a drink that is laced has been spiked and mixed up, so these letters are stirred together

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A drinker craves a bottle of cordial that has been spiked with whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for courage, not a container: the Wizard of Oz character went to the wizard to ask for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Wizard of Oz this timid character wants courage, which British slang calls bottle.

clue.text: One's thick slice of ham or onion

indicators.note: a slice is a portion cut from within these words, so the letters sit inside them

explanation.surface: Someone is describing a chunky slice of ham or onion for a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thick' is a noun-like description of a person, not of a slice: 'One's thick' means a person who is stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit is someone who is thick, that is stupid, so the insult fits 'one who is thick'.

clue.text: Waiter quite slowly cut drinks off the booze tab

indicators.note: to drink is to take in, so the musical word swallows the other letters
cut means the musical term loses its last letter

parts.note: andante is the musical direction for a moderately slow tempo
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
a tab is a tablet of ecstasy, whose drug abbreviation is E

explanation.surface: A waiter, moving at a leisurely pace, stops serving drinks from the bar tab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims the last letter of the tempo marking, leaving ANDANT; 'tab' is a pill of ecstasy, not a bar bill.
explanation.definitionFit: One who waits on or serves others, such as a pump or car park attendant, is a waiter in the broad sense.

clue.text: The same two places to find students

parts.note: a uni (university) is the first of two places where students are found
a form is a school class, the second place students are found

explanation.surface: Two venues where pupils can be found are said to be identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uniform is unvarying, alike throughout, so it means identical or the same.

clue.text: Tense and unhappy about work led by the bosses

indicators.note: about means going around, so the tense and unhappy letters surround the work

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
down means low in spirits
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Staff feel strained and miserable about work dictated by management.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarchical approach where decisions flow from senior management downward is directed by those at the top.

clue.text: Bar's free for one turning up

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: EG, for example, means for one

explanation.surface: A bar announces that it is free for anyone who happens to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A long raised strip, as of sand or a hilltop, is a bar in the sense of a ridge or crest.

clue.text: What lady seeking partner hopes to do for estate manager

definitions.text: What lady seeking partner hopes to do
definitions.meaning: read as three words, a woman looking for a man hopes to catch one gentleman
someone who manages a landed estate on behalf of its owner

explanation.surface: A lady looking for love hopes to find an estate manager to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: A person employed to look after farmland and property for an owner manages the estate.

clue.text: Paradoxically, it could be best!

parts.note: as a verb, to best someone is to defeat them, which is what the superlative of bad also means as a verb

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the poorest option might, oddly, be the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: The word that means the poorest of all is also a verb meaning to defeat or get the better of, so it can mean 'best'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a verb, the superlative of bad means to defeat, the same as to best someone.

clue.text: I heartlessly intended to eat sweet, liking sauce

indicators.note: eating means taking something in, so the trimmed word goes around the sweet
heartlessly means the central letter of the synonym is taken away

parts.note: meant means intended
pud is short for pudding, a sweet course

explanation.surface: Someone admits they meant to eat a dessert because they love the sauce on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes the middle A from MEANT, leaving MENT, which then takes in PUD. 'sauce' is cheek, not a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is cheek or insolence, so an insolent person, one given to cheek, is fond of sauce.

clue.text: Court favourite, it's understood, dined with queens

parts.note: roger is the radio response meaning message received and understood
fed means dined
ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a queen, so two queens give ER twice

explanation.surface: A favourite at the royal court is acknowledged to have eaten with the queens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' is a tennis court, not a royal one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss tennis great with twenty Grand Slam titles was a crowd favourite on the tennis court.

clue.text: Hit erotic author interrupting tour abroad

indicators.note: the author breaks into the middle of the scrambled travel word
abroad here means astray or all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Anaïs Nin was a writer famous for erotica

explanation.surface: A writer of erotica disrupts a foreign tour and makes a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges the travel word into RUTO, which the author splits after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To collide with something, as a car with a wall, is to strike it, a phrasal synonym of hit.

clue.text: Love old sandwiches middle daughter leaves for cook

indicators.note: two outer pieces sandwich a filling between them

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
Regan is the second of King Lear's three daughters in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: An elderly lover squeezes in a middle child before she departs for the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' is a noun, herb leaves, not the verb meaning departs.
explanation.definitionFit: This herb's aromatic dried leaves are used by a cook, particularly in Italian and Greek dishes.

clue.text: She-devil, one punching priest

indicators.note: a punch goes into its target, so the number goes inside the priest

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A demonic woman strikes a member of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth this monster, half woman and half serpent, preyed on children: a female demon.

clue.text: Big cheese spread coming and a round provided

indicators.note: round means around, so the scrambled letters circle the condition word
spread means scattered about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: if means provided that

explanation.surface: A big cheese is spread out, with a round coming if requested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges the seven letters into MAGNICO, which goes 'round' the condition word after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a Venetian grandee, the word now means a VIP or important person, like a big cheese.

clue.text: Element in language of oriental comics?

definitions.meaning: manga are Japanese comics, so the -ese ending, as in Japanese, makes a mock language name

explanation.surface: A query about which element appears in the language of Far Eastern comic books.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey metallic chemical element (Mn), and whimsically the tongue of manga comics, as Japanese is of Japan.

clue.text: Old Breton, a Republican, one Macron irritated

indicators.note: irritated means agitated, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A historic Breton, a republican, is someone that President Macron has annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Armorica was the ancient name for Brittany, so a native of that region was an early Breton.

clue.text: Unwind fuse in the plug

indicators.note: to fuse is to melt and blend together, so these letters are merged into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove the fuse from inside an electrical plug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuse' looks like the component in the plug, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax and stop being so serious is a phrasal synonym for unwinding.

clue.text: Budding head of narcissus on a bouquet

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its scent

explanation.surface: A narcissus bloom is opening on top of a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' suggests a bunch of flowers but here is a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just coming into being and beginning to develop is emerging, like a bud.

clue.text: Old man dressing badly shows fleshy bulge

indicators.note: to dress is to clothe, so the father goes around the other word

parts.note: papa is a father, an old man
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A father who dresses poorly reveals a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A small nipple-like projection of tissue, such as a taste bud on the tongue, is a fleshy protuberance.

clue.text: Spun suit jacket of optimum design

indicators.note: spun means turned round, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: to suit is to fit

indicators.note: a jacket is the outer covering, so the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A suit jacket woven to the finest pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spun' reverses FIT plus OM (the outside of 'optimum') together.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeated pattern or decorative figure in art or fabric is a design element.

clue.text: Drugs ring criminals run is gone

parts.note: a ring is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: is gone means the run letter has been removed from the criminals

parts.note: pirates are criminals of the sea
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A drugs gang of criminals has fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is gone' takes R out of PIRATES, leaving PIATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics derived from opium, such as morphine, are a class of drugs.

clue.text: Two short English kings behave provocatively

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: R (rex) and K (chess) are both abbreviations for king

explanation.surface: A pair of diminutive English monarchs act in a racy manner.
explanation.definitionFit: This dance move involves thrusting the hips and bottom in a sexually suggestive way, so it is provocative.

clue.text: Left back to warn of trouble

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
the end is the back of something

explanation.surface: Someone stays behind in defence to sound the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left back' looks like a football position, but it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To be an omen of something bad is to foreshadow or presage trouble.

clue.text: I turned on taps for patriarch

indicators.note: turned means read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taps are marked C and H, for cold and hot

explanation.surface: Someone says they switched on the taps for an elderly head of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this antediluvian figure, father of Methuselah, is one of the Old Testament forefathers.

clue.text: Where Galácticos played, following team of stars

indicators.note: following means the club comes after the team word

parts.note: a side is a team
the Galácticos were the star signings of Real Madrid in the early 2000s

explanation.surface: A team of star players following where Real Madrid's famous signings played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'team of stars' suggests the Galácticos themselves, but 'of stars' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal time is measured by the fixed stars, so the word means relating to the stars.

clue.text: Collection of voices paper's reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, signalling a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper says it has gathered a set of opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voices' sounds like opinions in a paper, but means singers.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of singers performing together, as in a church, is a body of voices.

clue.text: What shoots and leaves diner eats first

parts.note: rocket is a salad leaf, also called arugula

indicators.note: to eat is to take in, so the diner goes around the letter

parts.note: a luncher is someone who dines at midday
A is first, as in A1 or grade A

explanation.surface: A diner tucks into a dish of shoots and leaves first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoots and leaves' looks like a salad; only 'leaves' is the salad, while 'What shoots' is the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon that fires missiles, such as a bazooka, is something that shoots.
